chapter: Maple Leaf, own orchestra and rivals
title: Forming Charles' orchestra and its personnel
summary: He formed his own band with Todd, Sam Dutrey, Henry Martin, Sonny Henry and Albert Glenny, playing the Moulin Rouge.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you have any time in there in between where you were spotting around? Oh yeah.
Before I put up my own orchestra I was just playing with different bands.
But I didn't play that long because I put up my own band right away. And I went to play for the Moulin Rouge then.
Because La Marrunde was to be one of the winners at Tranchina. And he had left Tranchina to put up that business, you see.
Did any of the fellas that have been with you in the Maple Leaf band go into your band?
No ma'am. Just a, let me see who came with me. Camilla Todd that was the pianist. And who else? I think Sam Dutrae, yeah. Sam Dutrae came. And who we had on the banjo? Henry Martin. The drummer?
He switched to banjo then? That's right, switched to banjo. That's right.

Besides that we didn't, I had to pick up the rest. See I picked up Sonny Henry, you know. Oh I knew him well. Well he played with me so that, later on I picked up Albert Glennie, so I had my full orchestra right there.
Was it a difficult thing to determine who you wanted in your band or was it difficult to get them to play?

No I didn't have no trouble in getting the man. You didn't tell me the trouble? No because you see we had the Joe Wells. Oh yeah. I didn't have no trouble in picking the man because they knew me, you see, and those that were idols I wouldn't see them. I didn't try to get nobody from no other band. What about Red Dugas?
